title: Boss: the model shop
summary: Split, fit, evaluate, classify and cluster, all from scratch.

steps.title: The brief
steps.body: An estate agency wants three things from its data: a price model they can trust, a classifier that flags houses likely to sell above asking, and a simple segmentation of buyers. You build each by hand. Each step stands alone, so include the helpers you need.

steps.title: Honest split and a baseline
steps.prompt: Write `split_baseline(df, target, rng, test_size=0.25)` that splits the **rows of the DataFrame** using one `rng.permutation(len(df))` (the first `int(round(n * test_size))` shuffled positions are the test rows, selected with `df.iloc`) and returns `(train_df, test_df, baseline_mae)`, where `baseline_mae` is the test MAE of predicting the training mean of `target`, a plain float rounded to 2.

steps.title: Flag likely over-asking sales
steps.prompt: Houses that sold above asking are labelled 1. steps.title: Segment the buyers
prompt: Buyers are described by `budget` (thousands) and `size_wanted` (m²), on very different scales. Write `segment(df, init_rows, iters=50)` that
1. standardises both columns (mean 0, std 1 over all rows: there is no test set in clustering);
2. runs k-means starting from the standardised rows at positions `init_rows` (a list, one per cluster) until the labels stop changing;
3. returns a DataFrame with one row per cluster, index `0..k-1`, columns `budget` and `size_wanted` holding the **original-unit** mean of each cluster (rounded to 1), plus `count`.
